narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional profile.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. With over 11 years of overall experience, you are in a relatively small group—only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this level of seniority. The model sees this extensive background as increasing the likelihood you have stronger options elsewhere.

The second most influential factor is that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities clearly signals higher risk of departure compared to the 76.7% of stayers who reported no such offers.

Working against the prediction is the length of time you have spent in your current role. Your 6–10 years with this organization is longer than most employees the model expects to stay, and this stability pulls the prediction back toward retention, though not enough to overcome the other two factors.

The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether targeted changes in recognition, rewards, or growth opportunities could strengthen your commitment. You may also wish to reflect on whether your external options better align with your long-term aspirations.
